answer.message: You owe $24 in duty for 4 bottles of wine. This is based on the value of the alcohol and the standard duty rate for returning US residents.
You owe $3.17 in duty and excise for the excess vodka. Declare the items at customs.
You owe $10.50 duty on the 3 bottles of South African Pinotage. The total volume exceeds the 1.5-liter allowance, so you must declare and pay duty.
You owe $4.03 in duty and excise tax for the excess alcohol. Declare the bottles upon arrival.
You are allowed to bring one 750 ml bottle of Canadian whisky into the US without paying duty or excise tax. Enjoy your drink!
You are bringing two 50 ml rum miniatures, totaling 100 ml, which is under the 1 liter allowance. No duty or excise tax is owed. You may bring the alcohol into the US without paying anything.
You owe $76.00 for the second carton of British cigarettes. This includes $66.00 in duty and $10.00 in excise tax.
Cuban cigars are prohibited in the US and cannot be brought into the country, regardless of your age or trip length.

You are allowed to bring one 750 ml bottle of tequila (40%) and a pack of 20 Mexican cigarettes back to the US. No duty or excise is owed.

You can bring 1 bottle of wine (750 ml, 13%) back without owing more than $0.01 in duty. This is the maximum allowed under the duty threshold.

You're allowed to bring 2 bottles of gin (140 cl) back to the US without paying duty or excise. No additional fees apply.

Nicotine pouches are not subject to the same customs rules as alcohol or tobacco. You may bring them back as long as they comply with general import regulations.
As a flight attendant, you may be exempt from the standard alcohol allowance. To determine how much wine you can bring, we need to know if you used your exemption in the last 30 days.
You cannot hide alcohol or tobacco in your checked bag. All items must be declared. Hiding items is illegal and may result in confiscation or penalties.
